newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sells 78.5 pct stake in insurer CNIA.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sells 78.5 pct stake in insurer CNIA.

text.p: Morocco's privatisation ministry said on Tuesday it had sold a 78.57 percent stake worth 310.2 million dirhams ($32.6 million) in insurer Compagnie Nord Africaine et Intercontinentale d'Assurances (CNIA), mainly to a Bahrain-based group.
The ministry said Arab Insurance Group (ARIG) had bought 67 percent of the 1,650,000 CNIA shares offered.
The remainder was shared by two Moroccan firms -- Interfina, an acquisitions company, with 7.03 percent and Atlanta, an insurance firm, with 4.53 percent.

"It (Arab Insurance Group) has the ambition to become the first insurance and reinsurance company in the Arab world," a ministry statement said, adding that the company had branches in Tunisia, Hong Kong and Britain.
The ministry said it had commissioned French bank Generale de Placement Banque (GP) to invite potential foreign buyers to take part. It had received five offers of which ARIG's was deemed the best.
